findings.category: auth / account identity (regression for pre-fix data)
findings.where: be/src/routes.ts findUserByEmail (login) after the R20-A-01 fix
findings.what: If a database already holds the two spellings of one address as two accounts (the exact situation R20-A-01 could create: one row NFC, one row NFD), the NFD account's owner can no longer sign in at all. findUserByEmail returns the first row only (exact match on the NFC key wins, otherwise the first scan hit) and the password is verified against that single row. Both spellings now resolve to the NFC row; the NFD owner gets 401 'Incorrect email or password' for their own correct password, with either spelling, and cannot re-register (409). Before the fix this owner could sign in with their NFD spelling. No account can sign in AS the other (the other's password is still required), so this is a silent lock-out, not a takeover. The fix comment says 'no migration' and there is no detector (db:check) for such pairs. I did not and may not inspect the real DB; whether such a pair exists there is unknown.
findings.repro_curl: Throwaway DB, server on :4871. Register two accounts with different passwords, then simulate the pre-fix state with sqlite: UPDATE users SET email='lgé-x@x.edu'(NFC) WHERE id=A; UPDATE users SET email='lge\u0301-x@x.edu'(NFD) WHERE id=B. Then: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4871/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"<NFD spelling>","password":"<B password>"}'
findings.evidence: Rows id 61 (NFC, password A) and 62 (NFD, password B). login(NFC, A)=200 id 61; login(NFD, A)=200 id 61; login(NFC, B)=401; login(NFD, B)=401. Account 62 is unreachable.
findings.suggested_fix: In login, gather every candidate row (exact match plus the non-ASCII scan matches) and accept the first whose password verifies (keeping one scrypt of work for the constant-time property), or add a db:check/migration step that lists rows whose normalizeEmail() keys collide so they can be resolved by hand before shipping. At minimum run that collision query on the real DB before the demo.

findings.where: be/src/routes.ts findUserByEmail legacy fallback (GLOB '*[^ -~]*' full scan + normalizeEmail per row)
findings.what: Every login miss and every new registration with a non-ASCII address does a synchronous O(number of non-ASCII accounts) scan on the event loop. Measured on a throwaway DB: 20k non-ASCII accounts cost about 20 ms extra per miss (58 ms vs 31 ms for an ASCII miss); 200k accounts cost about 270 ms per miss, and 8 parallel misses pushed /api/health to 1.7 s median and 2 s max. Bounded in practice by the per-IP failure limit (60 / 10 min) and the 100 registrations/hour/IP, and a classroom database is far below 20k, so it is not exploitable at this scale; it grows linearly with the user table.
findings.repro_curl: Insert N rows with non-ASCII e-mails, then time: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4871/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"nobod\u00e9@x.edu","password":"wrong-wrong-1"}' versus the same with nobody@x.edu.
findings.evidence: N=200065 users: non-ASCII miss 262-306 ms (5 samples), ASCII miss 31-35 ms; health during 8 parallel non-ASCII misses: median 1674 ms, max 2050 ms.
findings.suggested_fix: Backfill an indexed normalised-email column once at migration time (or normalise stored rows in a migration) so the scan disappears; or cache the scan result set.

findings.where: POST /api/auth/register e-mail schema (pattern ^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$) and normalizeEmail (NFC only)
findings.what: (a) Invisible characters are accepted in an e-mail: '\u200b' leading, inside or trailing (zq-x@x.edu followed by U+200B) registers 201 because \s does not match zero-width characters. Such a user cannot sign in by typing the visible address (401) and the account prints identically to a normal one. (b) Compatibility look-alikes stay separate accounts because the key is NFC, not NFKC: fullwidth 'ｆｕｌｌ@', ligature 'ﬁle@', dotless 'ıdx@', 'İdy@', 'ß/ss' all register 201 next to their ASCII twin (this is the documented no-NFKC choice; the goal excludes unlimited homoglyph work, so it is informational). (c) Because toLowerCase() runs after validation, the stored key can exceed the schema's maxLength 200: 190 x 'İ' + '@x.edu' (196 chars) is stored as 386 characters; harmless but the bound is not the stored length. No two of these can sign in as each other.
findings.evidence: register 'zq-ceee18@x.edu\u200b' -> 201 id 55; login('zq-ceee18@x.edu') -> 401; register of the 190 x U+0130 address -> 201 and /api/me email length 386.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject default-ignorable / format characters (U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+00AD, U+FEFF) in the e-mail with the same helper used for names, and measure maxLength on the normalised value.

findings.what: The R20-A-08 fix made profile.user.demo true for both demo accounts and false for real accounts (verified), but the demo flag is only present on /api/profile and in the top-level 'demo' of POST /api/auth/demo. The user objects returned by /api/me, login (password sign-in of the demo accounts), register and auth/demo do not carry user.demo, so a client that reads it from those objects sees undefined. Frontend flow is unaffected (it reads the profile).
findings.repro_curl: TOK=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4871/api/auth/demo -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"role":"teacher"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["token"])'); curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4871/api/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("demo","absent"))'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4871/api/profile -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["user"]["demo"])'
findings.evidence: /api/me: absent; /api/profile: True (student and teacher); real student and real teacher: False.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add demo to game.me() (and document it) or document in OpenAPI that demo is a /api/profile-only field.

probes_note: Approximate count of HTTP requests sent to throwaway servers (:4871 CORS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:5173, :4872 default CORS and invite code, :4873 demo off): about 5,800 fuzz requests (4 seeds x 500-700 per script, schema-aware and blind, all 31 operations, including HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE and wrong methods), about 1,900 Unicode e-mail register/login probes, about 7,200 requests of 73 scored attempts incl. 20-way races, the rest targeted probes.
resolved_from_r20: R20-A-01 (e-mail NFC/NFD): resolved for new accounts. NFC, NFD, upper-case, NFD+upper and lower forms are one account: 30 parallel mixed-form registrations gave exactly 1 created and 29 email_taken; either spelling logs into the same id; the lockout bucket (ip+normalised e-mail) is shared across the forms (10 wrong attempts across 4 spellings: 8x401 then 429, and the correct password is then 429 for both spellings); other users and the accent-less look-alike on the same IP are not locked. A single legacy NFD row still signs in with NFC or NFD and cannot be duplicated. Caveat: see R21-A-01 (pre-existing colliding pair) and R21-A-02 (scan cost).

R20-A-04 (OPTIONS / 405): resolved. OPTIONS on unknown paths (/api/nope, /, /api, trailing slash, wrong case, double slash, extra segment, *) is 404 with the JSON envelope; known paths answer 204 with a correct Allow header; POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/TRACE on /api/openapi.json and /api/health are 405 with Allow: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and a JSON envelope. HEAD mirrors GET (no body), is 405 on POST routes, and 153 HEADs over 17 GET routes with student, teacher and no token changed no table (row counts and rowid sums identical).

R20-A-06 (empty-object body): resolved. {} , '{ }', '{\n}', no body (no Content-Type), Content-Length 0 with application/json, chunked {} / empty / split, Expect: 100-continue, 'application/json; charset=utf-8', 'APPLICATION/JSON', whitespace-padded {} and unknown query parameters all give 201 (start) / 200 (reset) for the demo student; null, [], '', 0, {"a":1}, {"__proto__":{}}, {"constructor":{}}, BOM, trailing garbage, duplicate keys and whitespace-only with a JSON type give 400 validation_error; {} with text/plain, form, vnd.api+json or no Content-Type, or whitespace without Content-Type, give 415; 70 KB gives 413 (also chunked). Normal frontend shape (POST with no body and no Content-Type, as in web/src/lib/api.ts and the e2e apiCall) works for student start/reset and teacher reset. A student cannot reset another account: the body fields userId/email are 400, query userId and X-User-Id headers are ignored and reset only the caller; a real student and a real teacher get 403 not_demo; no token 401; teacher on start 403 wrong_role; locked mission 403 mission_locked; unknown mission 404. DEMO_MODE off: reset 404, auth/demo 404, seeded login 401.

R20-A-08 (profile.user.demo): resolved for /api/profile: demo student true, demo teacher true (also after login by password and after reset), real student false, real teacher false, a real student named 'Alex Martin' false. See R21-A-04 for the narrower remaining inconsistency.
still_open_from_r20: R20-A-02 (P2, design): unchanged. 30 wrong answers then the correct one still completes hem-01 with score 0 and returns the fragment.
R20-A-03 (P3): unchanged. After a better replay the older attempt result still says newBest:true, totalXp:0 while /api/me says 180.
R20-A-05 (P3): unchanged. 'GET /api/health HTTP/9.9' and a FOO method answer a bare 400 with no body; 401 still has no WWW-Authenticate.
R20-A-07 (P3): unchanged. Teacher A reviewed then approved bio-03, teacher B moved it back to draft, all 200.
R20-A-09 (P3): unchanged by design (8 failures per ip+e-mail lock the account for that IP for 10 min); the key is now the normalised e-mail, which closes the NFC/NFD/case bypass of the lockout.
R20-A-10 (P3): unchanged. Success responses are still {description:'Success'} without schemas; served spec equals the committed be/openapi.json; /api/openapi.json is still not listed in paths.
checked_ok: 5xx hunt: about 5,800 randomised requests over all 31 OpenAPI operations (blind and schema-aware bodies, nasty path parameters, junk query strings, wrong methods incl. HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE/PATCH, wrong Content-Types, oversized bodies, 5,000-char bearer, odd Origin/Accept headers, 3000-deep arrays) and about 1,900 Unicode register/login probes: 0 five-hundreds, 0 stack traces (server logs held only the start line), every 4xx on a non-HEAD request was a JSON envelope {error:{code,message}}. Status histogram for the seed runs: 200/201/204/400/401/403/404/405/409/413/415 only.

E-mail normalisation attacks: NFC/NFD/upper-case/Kelvin sign (K folds to ASCII k, same account)/'İ' (i + U+0307, distinct from i, equal to its own decomposition)/dotless ı (distinct)/sharp s vs ss (distinct)/plus-addressing (distinct and case-folded)/190-character local part (201; 196 chars accepted, >200 rejected)/NUL (400)/lone surrogate escapes (400)/leading, trailing, NBSP and BOM whitespace (register 400; login trims ASCII space and NBSP and signs in)/mixed case/reserved demo domain in any case (400 reserved_email). Random Unicode (combining marks, fullwidth, math alphanumerics, format characters, astral planes) 364 accounts created: every NFC and NFD spelling of a created address signed in to the same user id, never to another; no cross-login.
Concurrency: 30 parallel registrations of 5 spellings of one address gave 1x201 and 29x409; the UNIQUE index plus stored NFC key holds.

CORS / preflight: with CORS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:5173 the real preflight shape (Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method, Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization,content-type) on login, register, start, answer, hint, PUT profile, dashboard, demo/reset, classes students, PUT content status, openapi, health returns 204 with the exact Allow of the route, Access-Control-Allow-Origin echoing the origin, Allow-Methods GET, POST, PUT, OPTIONS, Allow-Headers Authorization, Content-Type, Max-Age 600, Expose-Headers Retry-After, Vary: Origin. Other origins (localhost:5173, evil, null, prefix lookalike, upper-case, trailing slash) get 204 with Allow but no Access-Control-Allow-Origin. With the default CORS_ORIGIN (*, as in the Playwright apiCommand) every origin gets '*'. 404/405 error responses also carry the CORS headers. Note for operators: the .env.example origin (localhost:5173) will not match a page opened as http://127.0.0.1:5173.

Score integrity: 73 completed attempts (6 fresh students, hem/mic/bio chains, about 30 percent replayed, odd students with 20-way hint races, 20-way wrong-answer races and 20-way mixed correct/wrong/hint races per step). Through the API: result.ledger sum == result.score; stats.wrong and stats.hints == the number of 200 wrong answers and hints actually accepted; /api/me xp == sum of the best score per mission. Read-only reconciliation of the throwaway DB: ledger sum == attempts.score == result_json.score for all 73; wrong_total/hints_total == step_results sums == answer_log/hint_log counts; mission_best.best_score == max attempt score == sum(xp_events) for every user/mission; best_attempt score matches; no negative scores; PRAGMA integrity_check ok, foreign_key_check empty. Mixed races never accepted more than one correct answer per step (others 409 wrong_step / attempt_finished); hint races charge exactly the available hint levels (rest 409 no_more_hints). Locked mission start: 403 mission_locked; unknown mission 404.
Auth/roles regression: no token 401; garbage and 5,000-char bearer 401; student on teacher routes and teacher on student routes 403 wrong_role (fuzz with role-matched and mismatched tokens).
Security headers still on every response (Cache-Control no-store, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, no-referrer, CSP default-src 'none'); no Set-Cookie.

Isolation: the servers ran on ports 4871 to 4873 with throwaway SQLite files in the scratchpad (confirmed with lsof); be/data and be/backups were not opened. Servers killed and the temp directory deleted at the end.
